eight miles further, and at three in the morning of the 10th
were compelled to halt from downright exhaustion and
fatigue. The horses and sheep were knocked up. The
poor boy was so tired and sleepy that he could scarcely sit
upon his horse, and I found myself actually dozing as I
walked: mechanically my legs kept moving forwards, but
my eyes were every now and then closed in forgetfulness of
all around me, until I was suddenly thrown down by get-
ting entangled amongst the scrub, or aroused by a severe
blow across the face from the recoil of a bough after the
passage of the boy's horse. I now judged we had come
about ninety-three miles from Yeerkum-ban-kauwe, and
hoped that we could not be very far from water. Having
tied up the horses for an hour or two, and without making
a fire, or even unrolling our cloaks to cover us, we stretched
ourselves on the ground, and were in a few moments fast
asleep.
"March 10.—At five we were again on our route, every
moment expecting to see a break in the line of cliffs along
which we had now travelled so far. Alas! they still con-
tinued stretching as far as the eye could see to the west-
ward, and as fast as we arrived at one point which had
bounded our vision (and beyond which we hoped a change
might occur), it was but to be met with the view of another
beyond. Distressing and fatal as the continuance of these
cliffs might prove to us, there was a grandeur and sub-
limity in their appearance that was most imposing, and
which struck me with admiration. Stretching out before
us in lofty unbroken outline, they presented the singular
and romantic appearance of massive battlements of masonry,
supported by huge buttresses, and glittering in the morn-
ing sun which had now risen upon them, and made the
scene beautiful even amidst the dangers and anxieties of
our situation."
In a direct line of upwards of 800 miles thus
gone over by Mr Eyre, there does not seem to
have been a watercourse, or a hollow of any kind,
crossed; and not a drop of fresh water accessible
on the surface. It could only be obtained by dig-
ging close to the sea-shore, or the sand-hills of the
coast; and even by that means was often not pro-
curable for distances of 160 miles together. The
dreary waste is described by Mr Eyre as an almost
uniform table land of fossil formation, with an ele-
vation of from three to five hundred feet; covered
for the most part by dense impenetrable scrubs,
and only varied on its surface by occasional sandy
or rocky undulations. The dangers and sufferings
of travel in such a region may be conceived; as
well as its generally uninteresting character. But
every now and then a startling little trait occurs
which gives the living touch of reality to the scene;
and again carries the reader forward, watchful and
anxious for the traveller. In the following for
instance.
" . . . I occupied myself in writing and charting during
the day, and at night amused myself in taking stellar obser-
vations for latitude. I had already taken the altitude of Vega,
and deduced the latitude to be 32 deg. 3 min. 23 sec. S.;
leaving my artificial horizon on the ground outside whilst I
remained in the tent waiting until Altair came to the meri-
dian, I then took my sextant and went out to observe this
star also; but upon putting down my hand to take hold of
the horizon-glass in order to wipe the dew off, my fingers
went into the quicksilver—the horizon-glass was gone, and
also the piece of canvas I had put on the ground to lie down
upon whilst observing so low an altitude as that of Vega.
Searching a little more, I missed a spade, a parcel of horse-
shoes, an axe, a tin dish, some ropes, a grubbing-hoe, and
several smaller things which had been left outside the tent,
as not being likely to take any injury from the damp. It
was evident I was surrounded by natives, who had stolen
all these things during the short time I had been in my tent,
certainly not exceeding half an hour. The night was very
windy, and I had heard nothing; besides, I was encamped
in the midst of a very dense brush of large wide-spreading
tea-trees and other bushes, any of which would afford a
screen for a considerable number of natives. In daylight it
was impossible to see many yards in distance, and nothing
could be discerned at night. . . . As soon as I
missed my horizon-glass, and entertained the suspicion
of natives being about, I hurried into the tent, and
lighting a large blue light, run with it rapidly through
the bushes around me. The effect of this was very beauti-
ful amidst the darkness and gloom of the woods, and for a
great distance in every direction objects could be seen as
well as by day: the natives, however, were gone; and I
could only console myself by firing a couple of balls after
them through the underwood, to warn them of the danger
of intruding upon me again. I then put everything which
had been left outside into the tent, and kept watch for an
hour or two; but my visitors came no more. . . . Rising
very early, I set to work with an axe to clear away the
bushes from around my tent. I now discovered that the
natives had been concealed behind a large tea-tree not
twenty yards from the tent: there were numerous foot-
marks there, and the remains of fire-sticks which they had
brought with them, for a native rarely moves at night with-
out fire."
Mr Eyre seems to have no hope, in spite of
Capt. Sturt's cheering dispatches, that any inland
sea will ever be ultimately discovered behind this
vast unpromising table land. Can it be, he asks,
that the whole is one immense interminable desert,
"or an alternation of deserts and shallow lakes?"
Incidental to the narrative of the expeditions
are many illustrations of native character: but Mr
Eyre, as we before said, has collected all his many
years' experiences on this head into a separate
treatise or dissertation at the close of his work. The reader interested in the subject will find his
information curious and ample. The matters
treated of embrace not only the physical and moral
state of the aborigines; their habits of life, rude
government, and social relations; their language
and dialects; but also very interesting notices of
the effects of their contact with Europeans, and
some valuable suggestions for an improvement in
the system generally adopted towards them.
Our extracts are limited by our space: but to
even readers familiar with Captain Grey's excellent
dissertations, much of Mr Eyre's information will
be new and original.
HUSBAND AND WIFE.
"Wives are considered the absolute property of the husband, and can be given away, or exchanged, or lent, according to his caprice. A husband is denominated in the
Adelaide dialect, Yongarra, Martanya (the owner or pro-
prietor of a wife). Female children are betrothed usually
from early infancy, and such arrangements are usually ad-
hered to; still in many cases circumstances occur frequently
to cause an alteration; but if not, the girls generally go to
live with their husbands about the age of twelve, and some-
times even before that. Relatives nearer than cousins are
not allowed to marry, and this alliance does not generally
take place. Female orphans belong to the nearest male re-
lative, as also does a widow, instead of to the nearest male
relative of the husband, as was found to be the case in
Western Australia by Captain Grey. Two or three months
generally elapse before the widow goes to another hus-
band; but if the wife dies, the man takes another as soon
as he can get one. If a woman, having young children,
join another tribe, the children go with her; but I am not
aware whether they would remain permanently attached to
that tribe or not. Brothers often barter their sisters for
wives for themselves, but it can only be done with the
parents' consent, or after their death. If a wife be stolen,
war is always continued until she is given up, or another
female in her place.
"There is no ceremony connected with the undertaking
of marriage. In those cases where I have witnessed the
giving away of a wife, the woman was simply ordered by
the nearest male relative in whose disposal she was, to take
up her 'rocko,' the bag in which a female carries the effects
of her husband, and go to the man's camp to whom she had
been given. Marriage is not looked upon as any pledge of
chastity, indeed no such virtue is recognised. But little
real affection consequently exists between husbands and
wives, and young men value a wife principally for her ser-
vices as a slave; in fact, when asked why they are anxious
to obtain wives, their usual reply is, that they may get
wood, water, and food for them, and carry whatever pro-
perty they possess."
NATIVE MODESTY.
"Innate propriety of behaviour is also frequently exhi-
bited by the Aborigines in their natural state, in the modest
unassuming manner in which they take their positions to
observe what is going on, and in a total absence of any-
thing that is rude or offensive. It is true that the reverse
of this is also often to be met with; but I think it will
usually be found that it is among natives who have before
been in contact with Europeans, or where familiarities have
been used with them first, or an injudicious system of treat-
ment has been adopted towards them.
"Delicacy of feeling is not often laid to the charge of the
Aborigines, and yet I was witness to a singular instance of
it at King George's Sound. I was looking one evening at
the natives dancing, and who were, as they always are on
these occasions, in a state of complete nudity. In the
midst of the performance, one of the natives standing by as
a spectator, mentioned that a white woman was passing up
the road; and although this was some little distance away,
and the night was tolerably dark, they all with one accord
crossed over to the bushes where their cloaks were, put
them on, and resumed their amusement."
Some representations of native ornaments, wea-
pons, and implements and works of industry, in
this part of the book, are useful to the text.
THE THEATRICAL EXAMINER.
HAYMARKET.
The False Mr Pope is a retired Hammersmith
tradesman of about five feet four, with a Ramilie
wig and tail more than half as big as himself,
square-cut buckram skirts, long flapped white
waistcoat, and minute three-cornered hat, who is
passed off by a wag of a player upon a party of
petticoat admirers of Pope, for the celebrated au-
thor of the Dunciad. To fancy Mr Buckstone in
this predicament, is to have a very clear notion of
Mr Peake's amusing farce.
It is nicely presented; with abundance of pe-
ruke for the gentlemen, and of hoods, clustering
curls, cardinals, and little china, for the ladies; and
it perpetrates a vast many abominable jokes, which
nobody but the actors and actresses can possibly
be expected to laugh at. But this is the "moral."
The ladies are in such a state of frantic foregone
admiration of Mr Pope, that the more audacious
the flights of Mr Buckstone the wittier they are
taken to be; and though this is rather a danger-
ous experiment for a farce, the audience help it
ont with their good-nature.
Indeed it would take a troublesome amount of
the other quality to withstand Mr Buckstone's
practical points of drollery. When he takes off
his wig in a sudden heat, for example, and exposes
his small bald head, Swift's mouse under a canopy
of state is nothing to it. When he effects a series
of practical Rapes of the Lock, too, he uses the
scissors like a true poet. And when he passes
from doing to suffering, tastes the griefs as well as
glories of fame, and is well thrashed by Mr Culli's
chairman as he leaves the player's house,—the act
closed with a roar. There should have been no
second. There is nothing but stale repetition in
the second act. The ladies retort with a practical
joke of their own, which is much more remarkable
for its dullness than for any more lady-like quality.
LYCEUM.
An excellent new farce was played here on Monday night; better than any piece of its class which
we have seen for many a day. It has nicety of
character, and a good broad humour. You laugh,
and have no need to be ashamed of your mirth.
There is neither caricature nor coarseness. We
cannot stay to tell the plot (which is a plot, and
not told without some pains), but must briefly
counsel the playgoer to see Peter Jenkins. Mr
and Mrs Keeley, Mr Wigan and Mr Meadows,
complete an admirable cast. Mr Keeley is not
only an honest truth-telling fellow forced to tell
lies for a friend; but a confirmed little bachelor,
caught, willy-nilly, in the snares of matrimony.
His dilemmas are intense, and he does justice to
them.
FOREIGN NEWS.
FRANCE.
DEATH OF M. ROYER COLLARD.—This illustrious
citizen died on the 4th inst., at his estate at Chateauvieux,
near Saint-Aignan, in the 82nd year of his age. M.
Royer Collard had been President of the Chamber of De-
puties, Member of the French Academy, and Professor of
Philosophy at the College of France.
THE SLAVE TRADE CONVENTION.—"The vessels in-
tended to act against the slave trade are not," says the
'Constitutionnel,' "yet ready to proceed to the coasts of
Africa. They are not to set out for six weeks or two
months. Meanwhile communications are exchanged with
England every day on the subject of the mission which
the two navies are to fulfil together. Recently the Ad-
miralty has drawn up regulations for day and night sig-
nals, which the English and French cruisers are to make
use of, in order to mutually recognise each other. It ap-
pears that we have approved of all the dispositions of
these regulations. It is divided into two parts; the first
concerning sailing vessels, and the other steamers. The
English navy has been long occupied for its own use with
a regulation of this kind for steamers, collisions of which
are both frequent and dangerous. In France, nothing
has been done in that respect."
RUMOURED RETIREMENT OF MARSHAL SOULT.—A
letter from Castres announces that the Marquis de Mor-
nay has just arrived at Soultberg. If report can be be-
lieved, the marquis, who was at Beauvais for the Council-
General, quitted that town precipitately, in consequence
of a pressing invitation from the Minister of War. The
old marshal, who declares himself exceedingly fatigued
with the struggles and difficulties which he has to en-
counter, particularly from Algeria, and who is besides
tormented with a chronic cough, again talks of withdraw-
ing from office; but, as to withdraw at his age is to give
up public affairs for ever, he says, to
take such a determination without consulting his family.
The 'France' discredits the report of the Marshal's
retirement.
VISIT OF THE FRENCH PRINCES TO THE QUEEN OF
SPAIN.—On the 3rd inst., the Duke and Duchess de Ne-
mours and the Duke d'Aumale, after visiting Biarritz
and St Jean de Luz, arrived at the bridge which unites
France with Spain. There the Princes alighted from
their carriages and crossed the bridge on foot, accompa-
nied by Count Bresson, the French Ambassador, the Pre-
fect of the Department of the Lower Pyrenees; M. Aze-
vedo; Gen. Boyer, Aid-de-Camp of the Duke de Ne-
mours; Col. Jamin, Aid-de-Camp of the Duke d'Aumale,
&c. On reaching the Spanish territory they were com-
plimented by the Duke de San Carlos, a nobleman of the
Queen's Bedchamber, and Senor Arana, Master of the
Ceremonies of the Palace, in the name of the Queen, and
by Senors Olozabal and Aldamar, in that of the province
of Guipuzcoa. Gen. Barrenechea, commander of the pro-
vince, received the French Princes at the head of the
troops with all the honours due to their rank. The people,
on their side, loudly cheered them. The august party
slept at Tolosa, and entered Pampeluna on the following
day. Accounts from Bayonne of the 8th state that they
had returned to that town in good health, highly satisfied
with the reception given them, not only at Pampeluna,
but along the whole of their journey in Spain. The Duke
d'Aumale travelled back through the valley of Bastan on
horseback.
FUTURE RESIDENCE OF DON CARLOS.—The 'Constitu-
tionnel' says:—"The Marquis de Villafranca is hourly
expected at Paris. He comes to solicit, it is said, authori-
sation for Don Carlos and the Princess to proceed to
Rome, the climate of Bourges being injurious to the health
of the Princess, who was born in Brazil. If M. de
Villafranca does not obtain passports for Italy, he is
directed to demand from the French Government per-
mission for Don Carlos and the Princess to fix their resi-
dence in such town of the south as they may choose."
THE POPE'S SENTIMENTS TOWARDS FRANCE.—The
'Journal des Debats' states that on the occasion of the
celebration of the fêtes of St Louis in the French church at
Rome, the Pope and a considerable number of cardinals
attended. M. Rossi, the French Plenipotentiary, opened
the door of the carriage at the church door, and thanked
his Holiness for the honour he had designed to confer on the
French church. The Pope, in a voice so loud that he could
be heard by the crowd assembled around him, replied that
he had great pleasure in performing the pious duty, and
that he should be happy that that expression of his senti-
ments were known to the King of the French. After
prayers, his Holiness retired to an adjoining apartment,
where the ceremony of kissing his toe was gone through
by all the natives of France that presented themselves.

Det war en wacker syn att se den kraft- fulle unge mannen på det eldiga djuret; den tätt åtknäppta rocken wisade på det fördelaktiga- ste hans smidiga wäxt, och han satt fritt och u- tan twång i sadeln. Allra först lämnade jag den åt P. gamla wärdinnan, som med faknadens tårar omtalade för mig den fristliga färlef, du under få många år bewisat henne, då du flera gånger fjälfmant besökt henne med Guds ord, både under hennes hälsodagar och hennes fjukdomstid. Flera andra har jag hört med mycket faknad omtala dig; och det skall blifwa kärt för dem alla att få fjälfwa läsa eller höra för sig uppläfas de fifta viktiga orden, du i Herrens hus till oss uttalade. För fru F. skall jag och vid tillfälle, rätt gärna tolka desamma på swenska språket.

Uppmuntrade af detta hans lof- wärda efterdöme, och redan förut betänkta därpå, begynte äfwen wi, Rosengren och jag, att här Jo- hannedagen anställa dylika bibel- förklaringar, och ämma därmed fortfara hela sommaren, hvarje söndag, såvidt möjligt är. Dyre Fader! Nedaan flera år har jag warit på krigsstepp, Dock, på mitt nuvarande skepp fynes det, som om Pingstdagen förnyat sig; måtte Gud mer och mer utbreda sitt werf! Förra året gafs det blott tre på vårt skepp, som befände Herren; twå af dem hafwa såsom invaliden lemnat skeppet, blott jag allena blef qwar; Dock belöper sig nu wart antal till mellan 60 och 100. Mer än hälften af dem funna fröjda sig öswer fin Frälsares förlåtande nåd och färlef, och de hafwa fätt den Helige Andes wittnessbörd. De weta, att deras fynder förlåtatas dem och de hafwa börjat wandra liffens wäg i himmelft hopp.

Wi hafwa andliga sammankomster regelmässigt twå gånger hwarje wecka och hafwa walt en ibland öß till ledare af andaften. Bönestunder hålla wi hwarje afton, emedan på de twå regelmässiga sammankomsterna det hwarken är rum att emottaga alla, ej heller tid att funna tala till alla; äfwen förhindrar tjensten det, att alla på en gång skulle funna taga del deri. Wåra bönestunder begynna om aftonen klockan 8 och flutas fällan före midnatt. Sedan wi hållit bönestunder, bedja wi äfwen efteråt med botfördiga hjertan nästan hwarje afton. Helt nyß hafwa några befänt sig funnit frid.       <Heading type="running_title">
        <Line>CHARTER-BOEK</Line>
      </Heading>
    </Header>
    <Body>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>formeerde Religie, die uyt andere Gewes-</Line>
        <Line>ten en Landen genootſaeckt mogten weſen</Line>
        <Line>te vertrecken, en haer met haer geheele</Line>
        <Line>vaste wooninge binnen deeſe Provintie ſul-</Line>
        <Line>len willen ende effectivelyck komen neder</Line>
        <Line>te ſetten, ende haer als ſoodanige aen de</Line>
        <Line>Grietsluyden ten platten Lande ende de</Line>
        <Line>Magiſtraten van de Steden, daer ſy geden-</Line>
        <Line>ken te verblyven, komen aen te geeven,</Line>
        <Line>ende publycke profeſſie van de gemelde</Line>
        <Line>gereformeerde religie doen, voor den tydt</Line>
        <Line>van twaalf jaeren vry ſullen ſyn ende ge-</Line>
        <Line>laten worden van alle extraordinaris lasten</Line>
        <Line>ofte ſchattingen, die haer Edele Mogende</Line>
        <Line>genoodſaeckt ſouden mogen worden op te</Line>
        <Line>ſtellen, van wat natuyre oock die voor-</Line>
        <Line>ſchreeven extraordinaris ſchattingen ſouden</Line>
        <Line>mogen ſyn, ende daer te boven voor den</Line>
        <Line>voorſchreeven tyd geëximeert van de ordi-</Line>
        <Line>naris hooft- en ſchoorsteengelden, met wy-</Line>
        <Line>dere toeſegginge, dat die geene, welcke</Line>
        <Line>onder voorſchreeven Familien betonen kon-</Line>
        <Line>nen, meeſters geweeſt te ſyn op de plaet-</Line>
        <Line>ſen van haere laetſte reſidentie of woonin-</Line>
        <Line>ge, alhier ſullen genieten vryheidt van de</Line>
        <Line>gilden, ende hun handwerck onbekommert</Line>
        <Line>mogen oeffenen, ſonder daer voor eenige</Line>
        <Line>recognitie of yets te betalen; waer af, op</Line>
        <Line>dat een yegelyck kenniſſe mag hebben, en</Line>
        <Line>van haer Edele Mogende goede meeninge</Line>
        <Line>en intentie verſeekert ſyn, ſoo verſoecken</Line>
        <Line>ende ordonneeren wy amptshalven midts</Line>
        <Line>deeſen alle Grietslieden en Magiſtraeten</Line>
        <Line>wel expreſſelyck, deſen alomme te doen</Line>
        <Line>publiceeren ende affigeeren, ter plaatſe daer</Line>
        <Line>men gewoon is publicatie ende affixie te</Line>
        <Line>doen.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Aldus gedaen op 't Collegie binnen Leeu-</Line>
        <Line>warden den 16 October 1681.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>(geparapheerd)</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>B. Heringha van Groveſtins Vt.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>(onderſtond)</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Ter ordonnantie der Heeren Gedeputeer-</Line>
        <Line>de Staaten voorſchreeven.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>(getekend)</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>H. van Wyckel.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Naar een gedrukt Exemplaar.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Heading type="main">
        <Line>Reſolutie, op eene Missive van de Regeering der Stad Amſterdam, bij wel-</Line>
        <Line>ke de Ingezetenen van deeze Provintie van het</Line>
        <Line>recht van Exue ontheven worden.</Line>
      </Heading>
      <DateLine>
        <Line>Den 7 Januarij 1682.</Line>
      </DateLine>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line><Initial type="drop">I</Initial>s ter vergadering geleſen de misſive van</Line>
        <Line>haer Groot Achtbare de Heeren Burge-</Line>
        <Line>meeſteren ende Regeerders der Stad Amſter-</Line>
        <Line>dam, in dato den 22ſten October 1681,</Line>
        <Line>ſynde in effecte een reſcriptie op haer E-</Line>
        <Line>dele Mogende misſive van den 22 July</Line>
        <Line>laetstleeden, raakende het recht van Exue,</Line>
        <Line>luydende van woordt tot woordt, als volgt:</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <BlockQuotation>
        <Line>Edele Mogende Heeren!</Line>
        <Line>„ Wy hebben wel ontvangen Uwer Ed.</Line>
        <Line>„ Mog. misſive in dato den 22 July dee-</Line>
        <Line>„ zes jaers, en daeruyt geſien, dat onſe</Line>
        <Line>„ Ingeſeetenen in de Stad Leeuwarden,</Line>
        <Line>„ nochte ook in Uwer Edele Mogende Pro-</Line>
        <Line>„ vintie met het recht van Exue worden</Line>
        <Line>„ beſwaert; wy willen gaerne deſe beleeft-</Line>
        <Line>„ heydt met gelyke vergelden, en Uwer</Line>
        <Line>„ Edele Mogende Ingeſetenen en ſpecialyk</Line>
        <Line>„ die van de Stad Leeuwarden van het</Line>
        <Line>„ voorengemeld recht vry en exemt laten;</Line>
        <Line>„ weshalven wy ook alrede de nodige or-</Line>
        <Line>„ ders hebben geſteld dat Dominicus Theo-</Line>
        <Line>„ dorus Paludanus cum ſociis daer van ſal</Line>
        <Line>„ weſen gelibereert, ende alle anderen, die</Line>
        <Line>„ van Uwer Edele Mogende Provintie hier</Line>
        <Line>„ ter Stede iet ſouden mogen koomen te</Line>
        <Line>„ erven ofte beuren; van Uwer Edele Mo-</Line>
        <Line>„ gende rechtmatigheydt verwagtende, on-</Line>
        <Line>„ ſe Ingeſetenen diergelyke vryheid insge-</Line>
        <Line>„ lyks te willen laten jouiſſeeren, waervan</Line>
        <Line>„ wy alreede door Uwer Edele Mogende</Line>
        <Line>„ misſive meenen verſekert te ſyn.</Line>
        <Line>„ Waer mede,</Line>
        <Line>Edele Mogende Heeren</Line>
      </BlockQuotation>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Beveelen</Line>
      </Paragraph>
    </Body>
  </Page>
</HistoricalDocument>

<HistoricalDocument xmlns="http://example.com/historicaldocument">
  <Metadata>
    <Language>Dutch</Language>
    <WritingDirection>ltr</WritingDirection>
    <PhysicalDescription>Printed paper, single page from a larger volume.</PhysicalDescription>
    <Description>Ordinance concerning counterfeit coins and a new ordinance against Batenburger double stuivers, dated June 21, 1622 and July 6, 1622 respectively.</Description>
    <Script>Latin</Script>
  </Metadata>
  <Page>
    <Header>
      <PageNumber>142</PageNumber>
      <Heading type="running_title">
        <Line>Placcaten van de Munte.</Line>
      </Heading>
    </Header>
    <Body>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Ende dat die alreede hier te Lande, overmidts</Line>
        <Line>de gelijckheydt mette Uytrechtſche Schellin-</Line>
        <Line>gen, onder ende voor een Schellingh wert uyt-</Line>
        <Line>gegeven: Zijnde ſulcks eene Spetie van Con-</Line>
        <Line>terfeytinge, ende als Hage Munterije, nergens</Line>
        <Line>anders om gepractiſeert, dan om de luyden te</Line>
        <Line>bedriegen, ende te miſleyden, ende door mid-</Line>
        <Line>del van dien groot werck ter Munte te procu-</Line>
        <Line>reren, ende alle goede ſtercke Spetien, in al-</Line>
        <Line>ſulcke penninghen te doen converteren, ſtrec-</Line>
        <Line>kende tot merckelijcke ſchade vande Gemeen-</Line>
        <Line>te, ende Ingheſetenen deſer Landen, ende tot</Line>
        <Line>ſubverſie van alle goede ordre op 't ſtuck van-</Line>
        <Line>de Munte: <Emphasis type="other">SOO IST</Emphasis>, dat wy noodich</Line>
        <Line>geacht hebben den ſelven penninčk openbaer-</Line>
        <Line>lijck by afbeeldinge, tot waerſchouwinge, de</Line>
        <Line>Ghemeente voor te ſtellen, ende t'eenemael</Line>
        <Line>voor Billioen te verklaren, ghelijck wy dan</Line>
        <Line>den ſelven, by deſen voor Billioen verklaren,</Line>
        <Line>verbiedende dien tot eenighen prijs uyt te</Line>
        <Line>bieden, ofte te ontfanghen, op de verbeurte</Line>
        <Line>vande uytgheboden ofte ontfanghene pennin-</Line>
        <Line>gen, ende van het vier-vout vande weerde van</Line>
        <Line>dien, volghens onſe voorgaende Placcaten te-</Line>
        <Line>ghens de Billioenen ghe-emaneert: Ghelijck</Line>
        <Line>wy oock verbieden op Lijfſtraffe, ende Con-</Line>
        <Line>fiſcatie van Goederen, uyt deſe Landen ende</Line>
        <Line>plaetſen der ſelver, op den voorſz penningh</Line>
        <Line>eenige Materialen te leveren, ofte oock eenige</Line>
        <Line>der ſelver penningen hier te Lande in te bren-</Line>
        <Line>gen, willende de ſelve in de voorſz penen ver-</Line>
        <Line>vallen te zijn, al waren ſchoon de penninghen</Line>
        <Line>noch aen niemandt uyt gheboden oft by ye-</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>mandt ontfanghen. Ende op dat hier van nie-</Line>
        <Line>mandt ignorantie ende onwetenheydt en heb-</Line>
        <Line>be te pretenderen, Ontbieden ende verſoec-</Line>
        <Line>ken die Heeren Staten, Stadthouderen, Ghe-</Line>
        <Line>committeerde Raden, ende Gedeputeerde Sta-</Line>
        <Line>ten vande Provintien reſpective van Ghelder-</Line>
        <Line>landt ende 't Graefſchap Zutphen, Hollandt</Line>
        <Line>ende Weſt-Vrieſlandt, Zeelandt, Uytrecht,</Line>
        <Line>Vrieſlandt, Over-Yſſel, Stadt Groeninghen</Line>
        <Line>ende Ommelanden, ende allen anderen Juſti-</Line>
        <Line>cieren ende Officieren, dat ſy deſe onſe Or-</Line>
        <Line>donnantie van ſtonden aen alomme doen ver-</Line>
        <Line>kondighen, uyt-roepen, publiceren ende affi-</Line>
        <Line>geren in alle Plecken van onſe Landen, daer-</Line>
        <Line>men gewoonlick is duſdanigen uytroepinghe,</Line>
        <Line>publicatie ende affixie te doen, Procederende</Line>
        <Line>ende doende procederen teghens de Contra-</Line>
        <Line>venteurs ende Overtreders van deſen totte</Line>
        <Line>voorfz penen, ſonder gratie, ooch luyckinge,</Line>
        <Line>faveur, diſſimulatie ofte verdragh: Want wy</Line>
        <Line>tot welvaren vanden Lande ende de goede In-</Line>
        <Line>gheſetenen van de ſelve ſulcks hebben bevon-</Line>
        <Line>den te behooren. Gegheven in 's Graven-Ha-</Line>
        <Line>ghe, onder onſen Contre-zeghel, Paraphure,</Line>
        <Line>ende Signature van onſen Greffier, opten een-</Line>
        <Line>en-twintichſten Junii, in 't jaer ons Heeren</Line>
        <Line>duyſendt ſes honderdt twee-ende-twintigh.</Line>
        <Line>Was geparapheert <Emphasis type="italic">A. van Zuyllen van Nye-</Emphasis></Line>
        <Line><Emphasis type="italic">velt vt.</Emphasis> Onder ſtont, Ter Ordonnantie van-</Line>
        <Line>de Hoogh-ghemelte Heeren Staten Gene-</Line>
        <Line>rael. Gheteeckent <Emphasis type="italic">C. Aerſſen.</Emphasis> Zijnde daer</Line>
        <Line>op ghedruckt het Contre-zeghel der ſelver</Line>
        <Line>Heeren Staten, in rooden Waffche.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Heading type="main">
        <Line>Placcaet tegens de Batenburger dubbelde Stuyvers.</Line>
      </Heading>
      <DateLine>
        <Line>Den 6 Iulii 1622.</Line>
      </DateLine>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line><Initial type="drop">D</Initial>E Staten Generael der Vereenigde Pro-</Line>
        <Line>vintien, Allen den genen die deſe jegen-</Line>
        <Line>woordige ſullen ſien ofte hooren leſen, Saluyt:</Line>
        <Line><Emphasis type="other">DOEN TE WETEN</Emphasis>: Zijnde ons leſt</Line>
        <Line>Placcaet tegens ſekeren vijf ſtuyvers penning</Line>
        <Line>(ſoo die weſen ſoude) tot Batenborgh onlangs</Line>
        <Line>gheſlagen, ende na den Uytrechtſchen Schel-</Line>
        <Line>lingh opſetlijck ghecontrefeyt, naeuw'lijcks</Line>
        <Line>uytten Druck ghekomen, hebben wy onder-</Line>
        <Line>vonden ende vernomen, dat by die van Baten-</Line>
        <Line>borgh (even of het niet ghenoech'en waer, het</Line>
        <Line>eene miſbruyck begangen te hebben, ſonder</Line>
        <Line>'t ſelve met een ander ende meerder te verghe-</Line>
        <Line>ſelſchappen) beneffens, ofte korts aen den</Line>
        <Line>voornoemden vijf ſtuyvers penningh, geſlagen</Line>
        <Line>ende gemunt is eenen dubbelen Stuyvers pen-</Line>
        <Line>ningh, onſe dubbele Stuyvers hier te Lande</Line>
        <Line>leſt geſlagen, in grootte ende fatſoen ſoo ge-</Line>
        <Line>lijck, datmen den ſelven uyt de onſe Hier-</Line>
        <Line>landtſche dubbele Stuyvers, ſonder te vooren</Line>
        <Line>daer van ghewaerſchout te zijn, niet onder-</Line>
        <Line>ſcheyden en kan. Want al hoe wel den Leeuw</Line>
        <Line>(die aen d'eene zijde ſtaet) niet en heeft het</Line>
        <Line>Sweert ende de Pijlen, ghelijck d'onſe, ende</Line>
        <Line>dat de Letteren op d'ander zijde niet de ſelve</Line>
        <Line>en zijn die op d'onſe ſtaen (waer by het ſchijnt</Line>
        <Line>datmen gheſocht heeft het bedrogh ende het</Line>
        <Line>arch voor-nemen te verbloemen, ende als te</Line>
        <Line>excuſeren) Nochtans dewijl ſulcke ken-teyc-</Line>
        <Line>kenen foo doncker ende on-uyt-muntlijck,</Line>
        <Line>'t zy door 't ſlauw ſnijden, of 't ſlap aenpre-</Line>
        <Line>ghen, op den ſelven penningh ſtaen, heb-</Line>
        <Line>bende daer beneffens alle andere by-ſlaghen</Line>
        <Line>de onſe conform, En kan men de ſelve, ſon-</Line>

      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Unkarilainen hypoteekkipankki Budapestissä on lakipykälän IX</Line>

        <Line>emitteerannut 140:llä unkarin kruunulla takaisin lunastettavia kunnallis-</Line>
        <Line>palkinto-obligatsioneja.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Nämä palkinto-obligatsionit ovat niiden erittäin edullisen arvonta-</Line>
        <Line>suunnitelman vuoksi sekä niiden ehdottoman varmuuden takia niin laa-</Line>
        <Line>jassa määrässä kysyttyjä että ne vastaisuudessa, paitsi voittoja, omaavat</Line>
        <Line>kaikki edellytykset, että ne myöskin voivat tarjota huomattavaa kurssivoittoa.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Emitteeraava laitos perustettiin vuonna 1869, sen täysin maksettu</Line>
        <Line>osakepääoma on . . . . . . . . . . . . . 50 miljoonaa frangia.</Line>
        <Line>ja vararahastot ovat yli . . . . . . . . . . 32 "   "</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Laitos sen vuoksi, katsoen sen pääomavoimaan ja toimintapiiriin,</Line>
        <Line>luetaan Europan ensimäisten rahalaitosten joukkoon.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Alla olevan jäljennetyn arvontasuunnitelman</Line>
        <Line>mukaan tapahtuvat arvonnat 6 kertaa</Line>
        <Line>vuodessa, nimittäin</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Helmikuun 27 p:nä päävoitto . . 200,000 Kr.</Line>

        <Line>Lokakuun "   " . . 100,000 Kr.</Line>

      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Koska nämä palkinto-obligatsionit sekä arvontasuunnitelmaansa</Line>
        <Line>että voittoedellytyksiin nähden ovat melkoista paremmat tähän saakka</Line>
        <Line>olemassa olevia kuoletettavia obligatsioneja, niin on otaksuttavissa, että</Line>
        <Line>niiden hinta piakkoin nousee melkoista korkeammaksi emissionihintaa, kuten</Line>
        <Line>tähän saakka kaikissa obligatsioniemissioneissa on tapahtunut.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Vilkkaan liikeyhtey.emme vuoksi Suomen kanssa on Unkarin</Line>
        <Line>Hypoteekkipankki meille luovuttanut osan emissionia, nimittäin 10,000</Line>
        <Line>kappaletta niitä kunnallis-palkinto-obligatsioneja tarjottavaksi tilattavaksi</Line>
        <Line>Suomessa.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Esitämme täten julkisesti tilattavaksi 10,000 kappaletta näitä pal-</Line>
        <Line>kinto-obligatsioneja seuraavilla ehdoilla:</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Palkinto-obligatsionit tarjotaan alkuperäisen tilaustarjoumuksen</Line>
        <Line>mukaan 140 Unkarin kruunua = 147 Smkn hinnasta tilattaviksi. Tilattaessa</Line>
        <Line>on maksettava 15 kruunun = 15: 78 Smk jokaisesta tilatusta obllgatsionista,</Line>
        <Line>jota vastoin jälellä oleva määrä 125 kruunua = 131: 25 Smk on mak-</Line>
        <Line>settava helmikuun kuluessa 1907. Näiden 125 kruunun täydellinen maksu</Line>
        <Line>ei ole kuitenkaan pakollinen, koska myönnetään toinenkin 15 kruunun</Line>
        <Line>vähittäismaksu ja voidaan sen jälkeen jälellä olevat 110 kruunua, kui-</Line>
        <Line>tenkin niille laskettavalla tavallisella vuosikorolla maksaa vähissä erissä</Line>
        <Line>kahden vuoden aikana harkinnan mukaan.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Kun tilaaja on maksanut ensimäiset 15 kruunua lähetetään hänelle tilatun</Line>
      </Paragraph>

        <Line>Unkarin Hypoteekkipankin emissionit noteerataan Budapestin,</Line>

      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Näitä palkinto-obligatsioneja otetaan lakisäädösten hengen mukaan</Line>
        <Line>kaikissa Unkarin valtiokassoissa vastaan virka- ja liiketakuina ja voidaan</Line>
        <Line>niitä asettaa fideikommissi ja talletusrahoiksi.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Jokainen voitolla, katsomatta minkä suuruisella voittomäärällä,</Line>

        <Line>osaa seuraaviin arvontoihin, niinollen voi samalle obligatsionille</Line>
        <Line>langeta useampia voittoja.</Line>

      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Voittomäärät ovat maksettavat 3 kuukautta arvonnan jälkeen. Ar-</Line>

nales de Europa, como de la Cúria Romana lo testifica Nicolao de Lira, del Reino de Napoles, Sicilia Mateo de Afflitis, del Portugal, i otras provincias, Antonio Gama, i otros que plenamente juntó su Adicionador. De Francia Cassaneo, i de Saboya Ofasco, i Antonio Theslauro, que son dignos de verse para este punto.

I debe estar tan lexos un Oidor de enojarle con sus compañeros, ó quererlos mal, porque no le sigan, ó se opongan a sus votos, i pareceres, que antes elque es cuerdo, i lleva defeo de acertar, si defues de aver votado, viere que otros son de mejor, i mas bien fundada opinion, ó que dan mejor faída al negocio de que se trata, está obligado en conciencia a apartarse de la fuya, i conformarse con ellos, fin que en esto, ni por esto pueda incurrir nota alguna, porque antes la incurriará mayor, i con cargo de restitución, si coñociendo su error, persistiere en el consumazmente, por hacer puto de honra en no retraerle, como con ejemplos de la Medicina, i lugares de buenas letras, lo prueba Pedro Andres Canonheiro. Entre los quales pone el de Seneca, ya citado, que no es li- viandad aparcarse de un error conocido, i otro de Ciceron, que confiessa, que nunca pudo ser loable en varones avenajados en el gobierno de las Repúblicas, ef- tarfe siempre firmes en un parecer. Porque aun en un mismo negocio es licito mudarle, si se varian los tiempos, i las razones; i aunque no se varíe, reformando en mejor nuestro propio disfamen, como lo enseñan algunos Textos i Doctores, i en nuestros términos el Moderno Juan Brantio. I por esta causa, reprehende con mucha razón Cornelio Tacito, a Cesfonio Peto, que porque no pareciesse que seguía a otros, cuando votaba en el Senado, afeaba singularidades, i hechaba siem- pre por los peores caminos.

I mucho mas dignos serán de nota, i reprehension los que se dexan llevar tanto del odio, ó emulación de los compañeros, que por el mismo cafo que les ayan oido aprobar algun medio, se ponen luego de parte del contrario, cuyo mal natural, i los daños que se siguen de tales emulaciones, nota bien un grave Autor, trayendo en prueba dello varios ejemplos, i lugares de otros, i mostrando con evidencia, quan fuera van de camino los que tienen, que al Principe, i a la República le pueda eflar bien, que sus Ministros i Confejeros anden entre si discordes, i encontrados. Lo cual también trata, i refuélve elegante, i Cristianamente el Maestro Fray Juan Marquez, Melchor Junio, i Calisto Remirez. I este último añade, i prueba, que la pertinacia impide los buenos Confejos.

LAS EXTA advertencia seña, que si entre los compañeros, i colegas de una Audiencia, ó Consejo, que tienen igual autoridad, i potestad, es tan dañolo el mostrar afición particular a sus votos i pareceres, i gusto de que los figan, i el enojarle con ellos sino lo hacen, ó intimidarlos para que lo hagan, bastante se dexa entender, quanto mas dañofo será en los que en los mismos Consejos, ó Audiencias, no entran como iguales, sino como superiores, quales son los Virreyes, i Presidentes del las, que tienen, i hacen el oficio de sus cabezas. Pues cuanto mayor es su mano, i poder, podrán también dañar mas, sino dexan votar con entera libertad a sus Senadores, ó descubren, cuando lo comienzan a hacer, aunque sea con solo el semblance, ó otros leves in- dicios, lo que ellos tienen en voluntad.

Para lo cual traen asimismos infigues testimonios, i ejemplos Iano Langleo, i Juan Chier, notando los daños que esto ha caufado, i podrá caufar en cualquiera República, i Senado, i concluyendo que esta Ff es,

        <Line>قَوْسِ طه <Emphasis type="colored">قيه كح</Emphasis> بِالتَّقْرِيبِ وَقَوْسُ طه بِتِلْكَ الأَجْزَا <Emphasis type="colored">نز مد</Emphasis></Line>
        <Line>وَقَد اسْتَبَانَ انَّ الْجُزْءَ الأَوَّلَ مِنَ الإِثْنَي عَشَرَ جُزْءًا مِنْ فَلَكِ الْبُرُوج يُسَاوِي</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <MarginalNote placement="right_margin">
        <Line>لكِن ضعْفُ قَوسِ هَا مِايةٌ وثمانُون جزا وَوَتر هَا مايه وعشرون جزا</Line>
        <Line>ووتر ضعفِ قوس ط ه اذا بهذه الاجرا سته وخمسون جزا ودقيقه</Line>
        <Line>واحده وخمس وعشرون ثانيه فيكون ضعف قوس طه خمسة</Line>
        <Line>وخمسين جزا واربعين دقيقه وَطه بهذه الاجرا سبعه وعشرين</Line>
        <Line>جزا وخمسين دقيقه</Line>
        <Line>تتمة الحاسبه في بيان المعجم</Line>
      </MarginalNote>
      <MarginalNote placement="right_margin">
        <Line>قَوْس طه الى وتَرِ ضِعْفِ قَوْسِ صح اصل</Line>
        <Line>ها اَلتى هي</Line>
      </MarginalNote>
      <MarginalNote placement="right_margin">
        <Line>صح</Line>
        <Line>فيكونُ وَترُ ضعْفِ قَوسِ</Line>
        <Line>طه بهذِهِ الاجزا قا كح ک</Line>
      </MarginalNote>
      <MarginalNote placement="left_margin">
        <Line>حاشية</Line>
        <Line>وَقَد اسْتَبانَ انا اذَا ابتدَأْنَا</Line>
        <Line>مِن نقطةِ الاستوا كان البرج</Line>
        <Line>الاول من الدّايره التى تمر على</Line>
        <Line>اوْسَاطِ البروج يُساوِي في</Line>
        <Line>زمانه بالوجه الذى وصفناه</Line>
        <Line>من دَاىره معدل النهار سبعه</Line>
        <Line>وعشرين جزا وخمسين دقيقه</Line>
        <Line>والبرج الثانى منه يساوى</Line>
        <Line>منه تسعه وعشرين جزا</Line>
        <Line>واربعه وخمسين دقيقه</Line>
        <Line>من قبل انه قد تبين انهما</Line>
        <Line>جميعا يساويان منه سبعة</Line>
        <Line>وخمسين جزءا واربعة واربعين</Line>
        <Line>دقيقه ومن البين ان البرج</Line>
        <Line>الثالث يساوى في زمانه</Line>
        <Line>الاجزا الباقية من الربع</Line>
        <Line>وهو اثنان وثلثون جزا</Line>
        <Line>وست عشره دقيقه من</Line>
        <Line>قبل ان الربع باسره من الدايره</Line>
        <Line>المايلة يساوى في زمانه</Line>
        <Line>الربع باسر من دايره معدل</Line>
        <Line>النهار بالقياس الى الدواير</Line>
        <Line>التى ترسم على قطبى معدل</Line>
        <Line>النهار واذا الزمنا هذا</Line>
        <Line>الطريق في تبيان حسه</Line>
        <Line>هذا الوجه القسي</Line>
        <Line>من دايره</Line>
        <Line>معدل النهار المساوية في</Line>
        <Line>زمانها لعشرة اجزا عشرة اجزا</Line>
        <Line>من الدايره المايلة</Line>
      </MarginalNote>
    </Body>

<HistoricalDocument xmlns="http://example.com/historicaldocument">
  <Metadata>
    <Language>Arabic</Language>
    <WritingDirection>rtl</WritingDirection>
    <PhysicalDescription>Paper, 1 page, good condition with some ink bleed-through.</PhysicalDescription>
    <Description>Excerpt from a historical or religious text discussing figures such as Al-Khidr, Elias (Ilyas), and David (Dawood), with commentary and narratives related to them.</Description>
    <Script>Arabic</Script>
  </Metadata>
  <Page>
    <Header>
      <PageNumber>38</PageNumber>
    </Header>
    <Body>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>هذا الولد لا يشبهك في شىء فاصدقنى فليس هو ابنك فقال الشيخ للملك ان امنتنى على نفسى اصدقك</Line>
        <Line>فامنه فاعلمه بقصته وانه وجد عنده اربع ياقوتات فقال والله انه ولدى وعرف اليواقيت وكان قد كبر سنه فصرف</Line>
        <Line>اليواقيت على الشيخ الراعى واعطى المملكة لولده الحضر عليه السلام فلما ملك الله الارض لذى القرنين صار له</Line>
        <Line>وزيرا فلما دخلوا ارض الظلمة لطلب عين الحيات التى باكتاف الظلمة وجدها الخضر عليه السلام فشرب منها</Line>
        <Line>فهو حى الى خروج الدجّال وهو الرجل الذى يقتل الدجال ثم يحييه الله له ليغتر به من سبقت له الشقاوة</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <MarginalNote placement="left_margin">
        <Line>قف على</Line>
        <Line>الخضر هو الذي يقتل</Line>
        <Line>الرجال</Line>
      </MarginalNote>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>وليس على وجه الارض من ولى الاوله بالخضر معرفة فهو رءيس الاولياء ومقدم الاتقياء وقد عزا اهل بيت النبى</Line>
        <Line>صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد موته سمعوا قايلا يقول من زوايا البيت السلام عليكم اهل البيت ان فى الله خلفا من كل</Line>
        <Line>هالك وعوضا من كل تالف وعزاء من كل مصيبة فعليكم بالصبر فاصبروا واقتسموا ثم دعا لهم وانقطع</Line>
        <Line>الصوت فعرفا صوت الخضر على وعمر رضى الله عن جميعهم وكانا قد لقياه وعلمهما دعاء وذكر لهما فيه ثوابا</Line>
        <Line>عظيما فسمياه دعاء الخضر وهو لمن قاله دبر كل صلاة مغفرة ورحمة وهو يامن لا يشغله سمع عن سمع</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <MarginalNote placement="left_margin">
        <Line>قف على</Line>
        <Line>دعاء الخضر</Line>
      </MarginalNote>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>وفى رواية شان عن شان ولا تغلصه المسايل ولا يبرمه <Emphasis type="colored">الحاح</Emphasis> اللحين اذقنى برد رحمتك وحلاوة مغفرتك</Line>
        <Line>ذكره ابن ابى الدنيا فى كتاب الهواتف وانه والياس يلتقيان كل عام فى الكعبة ويقولان عند افتراقهما</Line>
        <Line>دعاء يوم عرفة بعد العصر وهو بسم الله ما شاء الله توكلنا على الله حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل <Emphasis type="colored">واما الياس</Emphasis></Line>
        <Line>فهو يونس بن متى وكنيته ذو النون وقد تقدم <Emphasis type="colored">وسبب</Emphasis> حياته ان شاء الله لما كشف العذاب</Line>
        <Line>عن قومه متعهم الى حين فهو حين اخبر به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وانما الخلاف فى حياة قومه وهو المشهور</Line>
        <Line>قال انس غزونا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى اذا كنا بفتح الناقة واذا بصوت يقول اللهم اجعلنى</Line>
        <Line>من امة محمد صلى الله عليه <Emphasis type="colored">وسلم</Emphasis> المرحومة المغفورة لها المتوب عليها المستجاب لها فقال رسول الله</Line>
        <Line>صلى الله عليه <Emphasis type="colored">وسلم</Emphasis> يا انس انظر ما هذا الصوت فدخلت الجبل فاذا انا برجل ابيض الراس واللحية وعليه</Line>
        <Line>ثياب بيض طويل جدا فلما رءانى قال انت من اصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قلت نعم فقال لى ارجع</Line>
        <Line>اليه وقل له اخوك الياس يريد لقاؤك قال علمت النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم فجاء وانا معه حتى كنا</Line>
        <Line>قريبا منه تقدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وتاخرت فتحدثا طويلا ثم نزل عليهما شىء من السماء</Line>
        <Line>وشبه السفرة بدعونى فاكلت معهما فاذا فيهما كفات ورمان وكرفس فلما اكلت قمت فتنحيت</Line>
        <Line>فجاءت سحابة فحملته وانا انظر الى بياض ثيابه فيها وهى تهوى به قبل الشام فسالت النبى</Line>
        <Line>صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذلك الطعام فقال ياتى به جبريل لالياس كل اربعين يوما فهو ياخذ منه ما شاء ويتناول</Line>
        <Line>فى كل يوم حولا من ماء زمزم <Emphasis type="colored">وقد رايته</Emphasis> على زمزم يقول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولنرجع الى ما كنا نذكره</Line>
        <Line><Emphasis type="colored">قال مقاتل</Emphasis> لم يكن قبل دوود عليه السلام نبى ولا ملك حتى يجمع الله ذلك لنبيه داوود عليه السلام</Line>
        <Line>قوله تعلى وءاتيه الله الملك والحكمة وعلمه مما يشاء <Emphasis type="colored">مكث في</Emphasis> الملك بعد قتل جالوت تسعين</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <MarginalNote placement="left_margin">
        <Line>قف على</Line>
        <Line>مكث سيرنا داوود في الملك</Line>
        <Line>بعد قتل جالوت تسعين سنة</Line>
      </MarginalNote>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>سنة <Emphasis type="colored">فقال ابن عباس</Emphasis> كان داوود اشد ملكا من ملوك الارض قال الله العظيم وءاتينه الحكمة</Line>
        <Line>وفصل الخطاب <Emphasis type="colored">وتوفى داوود</Emphasis> وهو ابن ماية سنة وملك سليمان بعد موت ابيه ثلاثة عشر سنة <Emphasis type="colored">او داوود وهو ابن</Emphasis></Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <MarginalNote placement="left_margin">
        <Line>قف</Line>
        <Line>توفى داوود وهو ابن</Line>
        <Line>ماية سنة</Line>
      </MarginalNote>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>وتوفى وهو ابن ثلاث وخمسين سنة وكما لم يحكم الانس احد مثل داوود كذلك لم يحكم الجن احد مثل</Line>
        <Line>سليمان وكان اذا غضب على احد من العافاريت سجنه فى قمقوم من نحاس وصب عليه بمذاب من</Line>
      </Paragraph>
    </Body>
  </Page>
</HistoricalDocument>

<HistoricalDocument xmlns="http://example.com/historicaldocument">
  <Metadata>
    <Language>Arabic</Language>
    <WritingDirection>rtl</WritingDirection>
    <PhysicalDescription>Single sheet of paper, handwritten in black ink.</PhysicalDescription>
    <Description>Letter discussing church affairs, a dispute with an individual, and instructions to a recipient regarding a new delegate and other matters.</Description>
    <Script>Arabic</Script>
  </Metadata>
  <Page>
    <Body>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>هذه المعاملة الشواذيَة وعدم تقيده بقانون الج. ونحن</Line>
        <Line>اليوم بعد ان قطعنا الرجا منه وبعد ان ذهب اليه البعض</Line>
        <Line>من الاساقفة لينصحوه فلم يسَمع لهم بل صاير له عارض</Line>
        <Line>جنون كل مرّة تكلم احد عنا. نهيءَ تقريراً للمجمع المقدسَ</Line>
        <Line>عن الحالة. ونطلب تأليف محكمة عليا لا تكون تحت تأثير</Line>
        <Line>غبطته. تحكم بيننا وبينه.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>يقتضي ان تسَتلموا المفوض الجديد لدى رجوعه الى باريز</Line>
        <Line>وتفهموه اللازم بخصوص الدباسَ وخلافه وبخصوص كل مسَائلنا</Line>
        <Line>ليعجل بحل الامور وانها المشاكل. فنتكل عليكم بذلك</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>وصل تحريركم لجورج ابن اختكم. واحضره الينا. وكما قلنا لكم</Line>
        <Line>نحن الان نقابل الحوادث بكل هدوء وسَكينة يكفينا الآن</Line>
        <Line>هم غبطته.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>سَلامنا على سَائر الاصدقا عندكم وطال عزيز بقاكم</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <DateLine>
        <Line>٣١ تموز ٩٣٦</Line>
      </DateLine>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>الداعى اخوكم</Line>
        <Line>المطران</Line>
        <Line>اغناطيوس</Line>
        <Line>مبارك</Line>
      </Paragraph>
    </Body>
  </Page>
</HistoricalDocument>

  <Page>
    <Body>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ<Emphasis type="colored">۝</Emphasis> وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ الَّذِينَ اعْتَدَوْا مِنكُمْ فِي</Line>
        <Line>السَّبْتِ فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ<Emphasis type="colored">ۚ</Emphasis><Emphasis type="colored">۝</Emphasis> فَجَعَلْنَاهَا</Line>
        <Line>نَكَالًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَمَا خَلْفَهَا وَمَوْعِظَةً لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ<Emphasis type="colored">۝</Emphasis></Line>
        <Line>وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تَذْبَحُوا بَقَرَةً<Emphasis type="colored">۝</Emphasis></Line>
        <Line>قَالُوٓا أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوًا<Emphasis type="colored">ۖ</Emphasis> قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ أَنْ أَكُونَ</Line>
        <Line>مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ<Emphasis type="colored">۝</Emphasis> قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ<Emphasis type="colored">۝</Emphasis></Line>
        <Line>قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا فَارِضٌ<Emphasis type="colored">ۙ</Emphasis> وَلَا بِكْرٌ<Emphasis type="colored">ۖ</Emphasis> عَوَانٌ</Line>
        <Line>ۢبَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ<Emphasis type="colored">ۖ</Emphasis> فَافْعَلُوا مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ<Emphasis type="colored">۝</Emphasis> قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ</Line>
        <Line>يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا لَوْنُهَا<Emphasis type="colored">ۖ</Emphasis> قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَآءُ<Emphasis type="colored">ۙ</Emphasis></Line>
        <Line>فَاقِعٌ لَّوْنُهَا تَسُرُّ النَّاظِرِينَ<Emphasis type="colored">۝</Emphasis> قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ</Line>
        <Line>يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ إِنَّ الْبَقَرَ تَشَابَهَ عَلَيْنَا<Emphasis type="colored">ۚ</Emphasis> وَإِنَّآ إِن شَآءَ</Line>
        <Line>اللَّهُ لَمُهْتَدُونَ<Emphasis type="colored">۝</Emphasis> قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا ذَلُولٌ<Emphasis type="colored">ۙ</Emphasis></Line>
        <Line>تُثِيرُ الْأَرْضَ وَلَا تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ<Emphasis type="colored">ۚ</Emphasis> مُسَلَّمَةٌ لَّا شِيَةَ<Emphasis type="colored">ۙ</Emphasis> فِيهَا<Emphasis type="colored">ۗ</Emphasis></Line>
        <Line>قَالُوا الْـَٰٔنَ جِئْتَ بِالْحَقِّ<Emphasis type="colored">ۖ</Emphasis> فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُوا يَفْعَلُونَ<Emphasis type="colored">۝</Emphasis></Line>
        <Line>وَإِذْ قَتَلْتُمْ نَفْسًا فَادَّارَأْتُمْ فِيهَا<Emphasis type="colored">ۖ</Emphasis> وَاللَّهُ مُخْرِجٌ مَّا كُنتُمْ</Line>
      </Paragraph>

        <Line>رَحمة وَ شهادَة <Emphasis type="colored">قَالَ الامَامُ احمَدُ</Emphasis> نا يزيدُ هُو ابنُ هَرُون قال</Line>
        <Line>نا مُسلم بن عُبَيد <Emphasis type="colored">قَالَ</Emphasis> سَمِعتُ ابا عَسيب مَولى رَسُول الله صَلى</Line>
        <Line>اللهُ عَليه و سَلم يحدث عَن رَسُولِ اللهِ صَلى اللهُ عَلَيه و سَلم اتانى حَبْرىلُ عليه</Line>
        <Line>السَلام بالحمَى وَ الطَاعُون فامسكتُ الحمََى بالمدينَة و ارسَلت الطَاعون</Line>
        <Line>الى الشام وَ الطَاعُونَ شَهادَةٌ لامتِى وَ رحمة لهُم وَ رجسٌ على الكافرِ</Line>
        <Line><Emphasis type="colored">قَراتُهُ</Emphasis> عَاليًا عَلى اُم يُوسُفَ المقدسيََه بصَالحيَة دِمَشق عن</Line>
        <Line>ابرَهيمَ بن صَالح بن العجمى ان يُوسُفَ بنَ خليل الحافظَ اَخبَرهُم <Emphasis type="colored">قال</Emphasis></Line>
        <Line>أنا خليل بن بدر <Emphasis type="colored">قال</Emphasis> أنا الحسَنُ بن احمدَ المقرى <Emphasis type="colored">قَال</Emphasis> أنا</Line>
        <Line>احمدُ بنُ عَبد الله الحافظ <Emphasis type="colored">قَالَ</Emphasis> نا احمدُ بنُ يُوسُفَ <Emphasis type="colored">قال</Emphasis> نا</Line>
        <Line>الحَرث بن محمد <Emphasis type="colored">قال</Emphasis> نا يَزيدُ بنُ هَرونَ <Emphasis type="colored">قال</Emphasis> نا مُسلم بن عُبيد</Line>
        <Line>ابو نصرة <Emphasis type="colored">قَالَ</Emphasis> سَمعتُ ابا عَسيْب فذكر مثله سَوآ لكن <Emphasis type="colored">قَال</Emphasis> فى</Line>
        <Line>آخرهِ عَلى الكافرينَ <Emphasis type="colored">هَذَا حَديث حَسَنٌ</Emphasis> وَ ابو عَسِيب بمُهمَلَتين</Line>
        <Line>وَ اخرهُ مُوحَدََة بوَزنِ عَظيم اسمُهُ اَحمَد وَ هوَ بكُنيتِهِ اشهرُ <Emphasis type="colored">وَ قَد</Emphasis></Line>
        <Line>وَ قعَ لنَا حَدِيثُهُ هَذَا بغلو فى مُعجم الطَبرَانى و المعرفَه لابن مَنْدَةَ</Line>
        <Line><Emphasis type="colored">وَ لفظُهُ</Emphasis> فى الطَبرانى فارسَلتُ الحمََا الى قُبا <Emphasis type="colored">و لهُ</Emphasis> حَديث اخرُ اخرَجَه</Line>
        <Line>ابنُ مندةَ و لاَ اعرِفُ لَه غَيرُهما <Emphasis type="colored">وَ الراوى</Emphasis> عنهُ ابُو نُصَيرة بنُون و مُهمَلة.</Line>

<HistoricalDocument xmlns="http://example.com/historicaldocument">
  <Metadata>
    <Language>Arabic</Language>
    <WritingDirection>rtl</WritingDirection>
    <PhysicalDescription>Manuscript page on paper, with text in black and red ink.</PhysicalDescription>
    <Description>Biographical entries from an Arabic historical manuscript.</Description>
    <Script>Arabic</Script>
  </Metadata>
  <Page>
    <Header>
      <FolioNumber>٣٣٢</FolioNumber>
      <PageNumber>٢٩</PageNumber>
    </Header>
    <Body>
      <MarginalNote placement="left_margin">
        <Line>بن عبد العزیز</Line>
        <Line>٣٣٠</Line>
      </MarginalNote>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>فقيل له فاغرمها له اذا فادعى ايضا سبق لسانه فقال له فاعدها فاعادها على نحو ما قال</Line>
        <Line>اولا فقال له فاغرمها فاذعن لغرمها واعترف وعلم ان برهان الولاية انطقه بالحق</Line>
        <Line>واخرس لسانه عن الباطل ويحكى انه قال للفقراء يوما لا يبولن احدكم في هذه الساحة</Line>
        <Line>ومن عاد يبول فيها عضته دويبة فغفل بعضهم فاتاها ليبول بها فمرت به دويبة</Line>
        <Line>كالريح فعضت ساقه انشبت به اربعة اضراس فاصبح متيما فاتى حلقه الشيخ فنظر</Line>
        <Line>اليه فقال عضتك دويبة فضحك وكان رضي الله عنه من اهل العناية فقال للفقراء يوما</Line>
        <Line>تعرفون ما يصنع بكم شيخكم يوم القيامة يحضر لكم عند الميزان فمن فضلت له منكم</Line>
        <Line>فضلة اخذها ثم يردها على من احتاجها منكم حتى اذا لم يبق الا من قصرت عنه اعمالكم</Line>
        <Line>فيقف لكم عند الصراط حتى يجوزوا عن ءاخركم <Emphasis type="colored">توفي</Emphasis> رحمه الله سنة ثلاثة وخمسين</Line>
        <Line>وتسعمائة انتهى</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Heading type="sub">
        <Line><Emphasis type="colored">سعيد</Emphasis> بن علي بن محمد الجزولي الحامدي اخو ابي زيد قال في الفوائد الفقيه الاديب الشاعر</Line>
      </Heading>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>المفلق البليغ ابو عثمان سعيد بن علي بن محمد <Emphasis type="colored">سهم</Emphasis> العريض النعم به وامام الادب العربية</Line>
        <Line>بالمغرب مرتسمى في زمام البلاغة بتمام الابداع وحسن الصياغة بشعره نافح اقصى</Line>
        <Line>المغرب اتاه وبسحر بيانه كافح جيش المحاورة فعاد ملك يمناه والادب له عبد يجيب</Line>
        <Line>متى دعاه وسهم يصيب الغرض متى رماه ودوحة اللسان بقطره بتلقيحه اثمرت</Line>
        <Line>وروضة البيان بتنقيحه امرعت وعطرت وقصائد شعره التي سحرت الالباب وفاضت</Line>
        <Line>فيضان العباب تشهد له <Emphasis type="colored">توفي</Emphasis> رحمه الله قبل الثمانين وتسعمائة بمراكش ودفن بها انتهى</Line>
        <Line>اخذ عن ابيه عن ابن هلال وعن عبد الوهاب بن محمد الزقاق عن علي بن موسى بن هارون عن ابن غازي وعنه</Line>
        <Line>ابو بكر بن حمد بن سعيد الجزولي نزيل مراكش واجاز له ما في فهرسة الامام ابن غازي</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Heading type="sub">
        <Line><Emphasis type="colored">سعيد</Emphasis> بن ابراهيم الهلالي السوسي ابو عثمان الفقيه اللغوي المشارك في الاصول و</Line>
      </Heading>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>العربية وغيرها وغلب عليه الادب واللغة له قصائد فصيحة وقطع من الشعر مليحة</Line>
        <Line>ورد قاضي الجماعة بفاس ابو محمد عبد الواحد الحميدي تارودنت فاستحقر شأنه فكتب</Line>
        <Line>اليه سؤالا بنظم رائق اوله<Above>٦</Above> الى علمك العالي مسائل ترتق تفطن لهن يا حميد واصدق</Line>
        <Line>فما الحكم في<Above>٦</Above> الاوزاغ هل ساغ اكلها وما الحكم في موتى المجانين فانطق <Emphasis type="colored">الخ</Emphasis> فعجز الحميدي</Line>
        <Line>عن الجواب فاحتمله الى مدينة فاس اجاب عنه ابو العباس المنجور وقدم في ترجمة الحميدي</Line>
        <Line>وفي تاريخ عن القاضي المكناسي انه <Emphasis type="colored">توفي</Emphasis> رحمه الله في العشرة الثامنة وهي ما بين السبعين والثمانين</Line>
        <Line>ودفن بتنزرت بالسوس بالمقبرة القريبة من القرية لا التي بها الشيخ حسن الشوشاوي بالغابة</Line>
        <Line>انتهى</Line>
      </Paragraph>
    </Body>
  </Page>
</HistoricalDocument>

        <Line>應正等覺聲聞菩薩衆㑹圍繞及餘</Line>
        <Line>一切有情無情品類差别</Line>
        <Line>尒時東方盡殑伽沙等世界㝡後世</Line>
        <Line>界名曰多寳佛号寳性如来應正等</Line>

        <Line>調御士天人師佛薄伽梵時現在彼</Line>
        <Line>安隱住持為諸菩薩摩訶薩衆說大</Line>
        <Line>般若波羅蜜多彼有菩薩名曰普光</Line>
        <Line>見此大光大地變動及佛身相心懷</Line>
        <Line>猶豫前詣佛所頂礼雙足白言世尊</Line>
        <Line>何因何縁而有此瑞時寳性佛告普</Line>
        <Line>光菩薩摩訶薩言善男子従此西方</Line>
        <Line>盡殑伽沙等世界㝡後世界名曰堪</Line>
        <Line>忍佛号釋迦牟尼如来應正等覺眀</Line>
        <Line>行圎滿善逝世閒解無上丈夫調御</Line>
        <Line>士天人師佛薄伽梵今現在彼安隱</Line>
        <Line>住持將為菩薩摩訶薩衆說大般若</Line>
        <Line>波羅蜜多彼佛神力故現斯瑞普光</Line>
        <Line>聞巳歡喜踊躍重白佛言世尊我今</Line>

    <Body>
      <DateLine>
        <Line>СОФИЯ 23-й Августа 1879.</Line>
      </DateLine>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Непоправимитѣ неудобства</Line>
        <Line>за отпечатвание и издавание</Line>
        <Line>на вѣстника ни въ Търново</Line>

        <Line>— Отъ двата града, Руссе и</Line>

      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>И тъй тука вече въ София</Line>
        <Line>започенвами съ този брой из-</Line>
        <Line>даваньето на листътъ си, за</Line>
        <Line>по-отборното съдържание и</Line>

        <Line>тукъ сътрудници каквито не-</Line>

        <Line>можемъ да посветимъ всичко-</Line>
        <Line>то си време за улучшавание-</Line>
        <Line>то му. П. Р. Славейковъ.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Heading type="sub">
        <Line>Отчислението ми.</Line>
      </Heading>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Въ първитѣ дни на м. августа</Line>
        <Line>бывшийтъ търновский губернаторъ г. Хр.</Line>
        <Line>Стояновъ ми съобщи една телеграмма</Line>
        <Line>отъ г-на Ѳ. Бурмова министра на вѫ-</Line>
        <Line>трѣшнитѣ дѣла и председателя на ми-</Line>
        <Line>нистерский съвѣтъ. Преписъ отъ тѫзи</Line>
        <Line>телеграмма азъ не взехъ, но мисля до-</Line>
        <Line>брѣ да помня съдържанието и́, което съ</Line>
        <Line>малки пропуски бѣше слѣдующето: „Ни</Line>
        <Line>едно правителство не е търпяло и не</Line>
        <Line>търпи да бѫде укорявано отъ своитѣ</Line>
        <Line>чиновници . . . . повикайте Славейкова</Line>
        <Line>и поискайте му объяснения за това що</Line>
        <Line>е писалъ и за намѣренията му въ</Line>
        <Line>бѫдуще“.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Попитанъ отъ г-на бивший губер-</Line>
        <Line>наторъ какво има да отговоря на туй</Line>
        <Line>запитвание, азъ казахъ за объяснение че</Line>
        <Line>съмь писалъ подъ влиянието на нѣкои</Line>
        <Line>мѣрки взети отъ министерствата, които</Line>
        <Line>азъ намѣрвамъ несъотвѣтствующи на</Line>
        <Line>конституцията и ухрабни за държавата.</Line>
        <Line>Много отъ тѣзи мѣрки, казахъ, сѫ и сега</Line>
        <Line>за мене необясними още, и ако могѫтъ да</Line>
        <Line>я оправдаѭтъ че сѫ въ полза на дър-</Line>
        <Line>жавата готовъ съмь да приема оправда-</Line>
        <Line>нието и да осѫдѭ себе си за пребърза-</Line>
        <Line>нитѣ осѫждения. Колкото за намѣрения-</Line>
        <Line>та ми въ бѫдуще по-смотреливъ мога</Line>
        <Line>да бѫда, ако бѫдѫтъ и министерствата</Line>
        <Line>по-осмотрителни въ мѣркитѣ които ще</Line>
        <Line>взематъ по управлението на страната.</Line>
        <Line>Синъ на България съмь по-напрѣдъ, а</Line>
        <Line>послѣ чиновникъ на правителството.</Line>
        <Line>Това немога да го забравя, и струва</Line>
        <Line>ми че ако го забравя ще бѫда не-</Line>
        <Line>годенъ синъ на отечеството а слѣдо-</Line>
        <Line>вателно негоденъ и чиновникъ на пра-</Line>
        <Line>вителството. Най-послѣ едно мога да</Line>
        <Line>кажа че ще ся мѫча до колкото е въз-</Line>
        <Line>можно да бѫдѫ справедливъ и осторо-</Line>
        <Line>женъ въ сѫжденията си.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Какво е отговорилъ г. Хр. Сто-</Line>
        <Line>яновъ не знаѭ; но азъ на часътъ те-</Line>
        <Line>леграфирахъ прямо на г-на министра-</Line>
        <Line>председателя, слѣдующето:</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <BlockQuotation>
        <Line>„Като гледамъ на обстоятелствата</Line>
        <Line>азъ съмъ желалъ и желая трайно ми-</Line>
        <Line>нистерство. Но какво е това направле-</Line>
        <Line>ние? какви сѫ тѣзи пристрастия? азъ</Line>
        <Line>имахъ голѣма надежда въ вашето пря-</Line>
        <Line>модушие, види ся преодолѣватъ. Ува-</Line>
        <Line>жавамъ запитванието ви (за намѣрения-</Line>
        <Line>та ми) но то зависи отъ мѣркитѣ които</Line>
        <Line>ще се взематъ.“</Line>
      </BlockQuotation>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Подиръ два дни бившийтъ губер-</Line>
        <Line>наторъ ми съобщи другъ телеграмъ отъ</Line>
        <Line>г-на министра-предсѣдателя. Преписъ и</Line>
        <Line>отъ него не ми се даде, но го помня</Line>
        <Line>почти до словно и той гласеше тѫй:</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <BlockQuotation>
        <Line>„Нека Славейковъ протелеграфи-</Line>
        <Line>рува прямо и ясно какво той предпо-</Line>
        <Line>чита: да остане ли вѣренъ на правител-</Line>
        <Line>ството или въ опозиционний лагеръ вънъ</Line>
        <Line>отъ правителството, срѣденъ предѣлъ</Line>
        <Line>тукъ не може да бѫде.“</Line>
      </BlockQuotation>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>На това азъ незабавно отговорихъ</Line>
        <Line>г-ну министру-председателю:</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <BlockQuotation>
        <Line>„Опозиционенъ лагеръ вънъ отъ</Line>
        <Line>правителството непризнавамъ, служилъ</Line>
        <Line>съмъ и желая да служя на отечеството.</Line>
        <Line>Развѣ министерството принадлежи на</Line>
        <Line>една партия и иска на сила да мя на-</Line>
        <Line>кара да му бѫда вѣренъ? прямо и ясно</Line>
        <Line>повтарямъ че ще остана вѣренъ на</Line>
        <Line>конституцията и на княза.“</Line>
      </BlockQuotation>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>На 12-й августа ми ся съобщи</Line>
        <Line>пакъ отъ сѫщото лице телеграмъ въ</Line>
        <Line>който се говореше за назначението на</Line>
        <Line>Д-ра Цачева губернаторъ въ Търново</Line>
        <Line>и въ който прочетохъ „Славейковъ же</Line>
        <Line>отчисленъ“</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Ето така стана моето отчисление</Line>
        <Line>което желая да знае всякой който иска</Line>
        <Line>да сѫди за него. Азъ съмъ принуденъ</Line>
        <Line>да обнародувамъ тѣзи фактове за да не</Line>
        <Line>би нѣкой, като не знае вѫтрѣшното</Line>
        <Line>лице на работата, да помисли кой знае</Line>
        <Line>за какво друго престѫпление съмъ от-</Line>
        <Line>численъ. Отъ този нашъ пазарлѫкъ съ</Line>
        <Line>министерството по телеграфътъ ясно се</Line>
        <Line>вижда въ какво съмъ се провинилъ азъ</Line>
        <Line>предъ г-да министри и за какво се от-</Line>
        <Line>числявамъ. Очевидно е че ако бѣхъ</Line>
        <Line>приелъ да хваля министерството и да</Line>
        <Line>го галя, или поне да мълча за неговитѣ</Line>
        <Line>не свѣсни мѣрки во вреда на държава-</Line>
        <Line>та, за неговитѣ нагли постѫпки и произ-</Line>
        <Line>воли въ ущербъ на конституцията; то мо-</Line>
        <Line>жахъ да си остана при службата поне,</Line>
        <Line>ако по други по-предни грѣхове про-</Line>
        <Line>тивъ г-да министри неможахъ да расчи-</Line>
        <Line>тамъ на тѣхното благоволение за по-</Line>
        <Line>вишение по заслуги и по достоинство.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Ако има прочее нѣкой да мя сѫди и</Line>
        <Line>осѫжда за това мое поведение, нека</Line>
        <Line>тури рѫка на сърдце и тогазъ да пре-</Line>
        <Line>сѫди: можахъ ли и трѣбаше ли да по-</Line>
        <Line>срамя моитѣ сѣдини и за едната си пре-</Line>
        <Line>храна да изневѣря на отечеството си,</Line>
        <Line>да ся отдѣлѭ отъ народа си, съ когото</Line>
        <Line>съмъ билъ до сега и съмъ му служилъ</Line>
        <Line>до колкото съмъ могълъ и както съмъ</Line>
        <Line>виждалъ за добрѣ, и какъ по семъ-сега</Line>
        <Line>да ся подзря да ида да служа на инте-</Line>
        <Line>реситѣ на частни лица, било то даже и</Line>
        <Line>за собственний ми интересъ.</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>Исповѣдувамъ че открай — си съмъ</Line>
        <Line>сиромахъ и бѣденъ человѣкъ, а сега,</Line>
        <Line>пострадалъ въ послѣднята война въ Е-</Line>
        <Line>ски-Загра, съмъ много по-злѣ отъ как-</Line>
        <Line>вото бѣхъ при гоненията въ турско</Line>
        <Line>време; тогазъ бѣхъ по-младъ и можахъ</Line>
        <Line>да мисля че имамъ прикѫтани поне нѣ-</Line>
        <Line>кои необходимости, когато сега лишенъ</Line>
        <Line>и отъ тѣхъ намирамъ ся въ съвершенна</Line>
        <Line>нищета, а вече застарѣлъ, при това и</Line>
        <Line>обремененъ еще съ многобройна челядъ,</Line>

        <Line>гамъ себе си на нови гонения; това да</Line>

        <Line>мисля да не съмь до толкозъ хинаетинъ,</Line>

        <Line>къмъ тѣзи които всякой който ги има</Line>
        <Line>знае колко сѫ мили и свидни. Отъ дру-</Line>
        <Line>га страна никой неможе да мя счита</Line>
        <Line>толкозъ глупавъ и наивенъ щото, ако</Line>
        <Line>би гледалъ само за себе си да не зная</Line>
        <Line>какво трѣба да правя, за да ся доко-</Line>
        <Line>памъ и азъ до нѣкой по-тлъстъ кокалъ;</Line>
        <Line>не може ми никой каза че не разбирамъ</Line>
        <Line>или ся не осѣщамъ какво ся е искало</Line>
        <Line>отъ мене и за какво, но азъ не мога и</Line>
        <Line>нѣма никога да пристана да любоугод-</Line>

Земледѣлческо образузвание на жената.

Една голѣма частъ отъ земледѣлческата работа се извѣршва отъ жената. Идеята на професоръ И. А. Стебугъ е била посредствата много съчувствено отъ рускитѣ жени. За да се удовлетвори жаждата на сел- ското-ступанското образузване, отначало съ се завзели, прѣди нѣколко години, частни лица.

    <WritingDirection>ttb-rtl</WritingDirection>
    <PhysicalDescription>Two facing pages from a printed Meiji-era Japanese magazine, 'Kokumin no Tomo'.</PhysicalDescription>
    <Description>Article discussing the difficulties of deploying military forces overseas, focusing on logistical challenges (transportation) and organizational issues related to conscription systems, with examples from historical events. This is page (一六) and (一三六) from Issue 27, Volume 3.</Description>
    <Script>Japanese (alias for Han + Hiragana + Katakana)</Script>
  </Metadata>
  <Page>
    <Header>
      <Heading type="running_title">
        <Line>第二十七號</Line>
      </Heading>
      <PageNumber>(一六)</PageNumber>
    </Header>
    <Body>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>四兵より、衛生、經理(給養)輜重一切具備せざるなし、</Line>
        <Line>故に其總員を擧くれば、人員三萬五千乃至四萬、馬匹一</Line>
        <Line>萬頭にして、是れ即ち一軍團あり、而して兵家曰く、</Line>
        <Line>此の一軍團以上は、決して海外遠征に動かす能はすと、</Line>
        <Line>今ま其理由を擧れば、略ほ左の如し、</Line>
        <Line>第一運送の不便 今ま試みに一軍團の兵を運送するに</Line>
        <Line>就て、幾許の船舶を要するかを概算するに、通常の大</Line>
        <Line>汽船にて少くとも二百艘以上を要す可し、若し夫れ渡</Line>
        <Line>海の便利を計り、騎兵を省略し砲兵の馬を減し、輜重</Line>
        <Line>を割き、充分簡易に從ふも、百五十艘を要するなる</Line>
        <Line>べし、</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <BlockQuotation>
        <Line>例千八百六十年英佛の支那遠征に用ひたる陸軍大畧二萬(佛八千英一</Line>
        <Line>萬二千但ー海軍上陸兵を合算す)に過きず勿論當時未た「スエス」の地</Line>
        <Line>峽通せさる時にーて不便多ーと誰も當時の戰記によるに佛國は商船百</Line>
        <Line>艘英國は百二十八艘を雇役ーたりと云ふ亦以て海外軍を遣るの不便多</Line>
        <Line>くーて船舶入用の多きを察するに足らん</Line>
      </BlockQuotation>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>以て兵を動すの困難なるを知る可し、</Line>
        <Line>第二軍隊編制上より生する不便 歐洲普通の兵制に於</Line>
        <Line>ては、其軍隊なる者は、土着編制にして、戰時一千人</Line>
        <Line>の大隊は、平時在營するもの四五百人なれば、而して</Line>
        <Line>歸休兵の有る場合ニ於ては、或は三百人ともなる可し、</Line>
        <Line>故に一朝事有つて其軍を差向けんとする時に於ては、</Line>
      </Paragraph>
    </Body>
  </Page>
  <Page>
    <Header>
      <Heading type="running_title">
        <Line>國民之友</Line>
      </Heading>
      <Heading type="running_title">
        <Line>第三卷</Line>
      </Heading>
      <PageNumber>(一三六)</PageNumber>
    </Header>
    <Body>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>是迄民伍に歸り、職業に従事したる所の歸休兵、豫備</Line>
        <Line>兵を召集せざる可からず、此場合に於て、全國の兵を</Line>
        <Line>動かす如き事に至らば、全國皆兵の主義ニよりて編制</Line>
        <Line>したるものあれば、誠に好都合なりと雖も、僅かに一</Line>
        <Line>部分の兵を動す事に於ては、其不便誠に少なからず、</Line>
        <Line>何となれば一部の歸休兵及ひ豫備兵は、これを召集し</Line>
        <Line>て他部の歸休兵及ひ豫備兵は、之れを召集せざるとす</Line>
        <Line>るが如きは、實際に於て頗る不公平の譯にして、且つ</Line>
        <Line>誠に爲し難き業なればなり、去ればとて現在在營の者</Line>
        <Line>を引上けて以て之れを派遣せんとする時に於ては、軍</Line>
        <Line>團、師團、旅團にして、其の軍團たり師團たり旅團たる</Line>
        <Line>の働きをなす能はず、即ち一の戰時大隊を編制せんと</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>するにも、數多の聯隊よりして、其兵員を充たさしめ</Line>
        <Line>ざる可からず、此時に及んでは、一軍團の兵を動かす</Line>
        <Line>時に於て、全國軍團の兵を動かす譯に立ち至る可し、</Line>
        <Line>去れば各國が兵を動かす事に就て甚た心配するも亦た</Line>
        <Line>謂はれなきに非ず、看よ<Above>トンキン</Above>東京事件の時に於ても、佛國</Line>
        <Line>よりして派遣したる兵は、即ち初度五千百卅五人、(此</Line>
        <Line>内にて西貢兵五百二十七人、南定兵二千二百人、海軍</Line>
        <Line>兵五百三十人、計三千三百人)にして、態々地中海を経</Line>
        <Line>て佛國より送りたる者は、千八百三十五人に過ぎず、</Line>
      </Paragraph>
    </Body>
  </Page>
</HistoricalDocument>

        <Line>वकंसेसं घंनं स म व्य क्ष्ी मा दि ॥ न खाधेसांमकुंयात्पस्परसुर सा हि ॥ शा न्य व या म वि झा ज्ञा न र कुं क्रिया ज्ञा पि ॥ सेंग्थ म लि</Line>
        <Line>त्मामाखोर में त्या ख्या ऊ नाज्ञपि ॥ गृह रू ध नि न र ल्वं कु सारसाधयेम ह ऊना ॥ मिसिनावि ञ्चा पिसा र्थ वाह्य पो धि का रा उ ज्ञा न प दा</Line>
        <Line>अभ्यास्वापीटिकाथेलिशिका रो षं वं मन्ये पि ला का थ स व दिरि षे र मा गु तो रा ॥ ग व ल के मा ला कृष्ण ख्ां स मृणा गा शा ॥ यथ क सं स म र्य शं</Line>
        <Line>त्वाप्रदग्वि भान्यपि ॥ क तु शा र्ग प्र भं वं ह स्ता ज र सि म टो म दा गं से कं सो मं पो ठं रु त्व ता यों स म स रु रा य धि वे ख्य प्र च्छ ॥ क स मा त्रं ख स मा हि</Line>

        <Line>मारव्य ग्रहृत्य मनी कं सं म द्वी ष निषदि ॥ ॥ न र रु ग वा न्ह क्ष्वा सर्वा न्का न्म प लि माना ज्ञा य स त्व स मा ज स्य क र्म स म पा दि गं ॥ ॥ ग त्व ६</Line>
        <Line>र्मा मृ नं पी त्वा स र्वै पि न प वो धि ता ॥ धा धि व्य र्या वं कै र्हिं सु मे रु प्र सा दि ता ॥ ते दा गं यं पि रू य्ह ग्वा न्ह म नो र्थ च रा व्धि स त्वा म्य स म</Line>
        <Line>कृत्य स मा ग्थं म्ये व मा दि गं ॥ ॥ कल्प ज्ञा म दा य वि ज्ञ्या सो गं व ध्वा प्र व जि तं सु मि च्छि किं ते प्र यु क्ष्वा ङि का रो शा स्य य थ्यू प न्ह र्हि स र्व धर्मा</Line>
        <Line>थे सि द्धि दा प्र ध र सा स ने वो के यं त्रि वा धि स म यं ॥ ॥ रु सर्व पा प मि र्का रा प जि ह्र द्वि म श्वा रा नि र्हू म वि म ल त्वा ना वा धि से वा जि</Line>
        <Line>क ढि या रा जि सा मा ज गं म्ह च्छा न र्ह त्वां व स्य व्धि ज्ञ य वि धिं वा धि मा सा स म्ब द्ध प द मा त्र य रा ॥ ० भू मि ला षं स त्वा ध्य य वा क्ष्कृ मि स ति</Line>

  <Page>
    <Body>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>यावत्तेध्रुवा संववखगात्रिभास्वर॥ श्िसिक्लसारविशमिरपिना्सगा॥ यवधिसदलामसाणिसुरपुर्णत्ु ्थयथ॥ कयस्िधाेते</Line>
        <Line>वलंद्गंणीय्विश्व॥ सर ति संका सशृ्तिति्दिमा्रूत् ॥प क सष्शयोाप्षत सर्य धाको्ियाकष ॥तमभ वा्िरण दूः</Line>
        <Line>धित्तासमाधि॥ श्षिप्य लंनोत्साह मन्त्र खं दो<Gap reason="missing" extent="string hole"/>बुंज्ञानानिर्मला यावद्यद्युत्खं विवोधियानिरुद्धं त्मानिर्म्म</Line>
        <Line>ह्न्माषवानां। णिविश्वाधिमासाद्य सव्वषयपदमात्रया<Gap reason="missing" extent="string hole"/> त्माकारसर्व्वधर्म्माणां वाधिसत्तो महामति</Line>
        <Line>संहरवानिर्द्दुःखानिर्मलात्मानरं साक्षाग्मिनिम्मिता राज्ञ्हं स्वेण व्यं सवाधिष्ठानपदमात्रया॥ च्छ्रां वचीरुनागश्च क्षोभ्माक्षोभिसां</Line>
      </Paragraph>
      <MarginalNote placement="right_margin">
        <Line>४१</Line>
      </MarginalNote>
    </Body>
  </Page>
  <Page>
    <Body>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>स्य कोमकाहखवि्णषम्त्लंवक्वामिभृग्षप ॥ वा्मी सितयूसुखा लनिरस मा्ि। ्कसमटंरामसरगनांवीयव॥ सयारथ</Line>
        <Line>कामरूप्येऽविमुक्ताग्र्योसौमृद्धिरस्वानिर्म्मासं। साद्य सर्व्वसत्वार्थं कृछ्योयायाकितेपुनः। तद्यथा रत्नलापद्यश्च सुवीवगाहुमगं भव्षिं</Line>
        <Line>व्रातयञ्चैवं साविमर्धना उम्भजिह्वा रज्ञापर सोपेय<Gap reason="missing" extent="string hole"/>ट्नावीकैग खद्युवास् याया इंगकैशोतं मद्धि सखाधयो। स्नानादिंभसना</Line>
        <Line>विर्वेद्याद्यपदद्वयं। गल्म्वादकनग्मञ्च वैकीर्णे न मिनर्पदा<Gap reason="missing" extent="string hole"/> भीमादकनङ्गकोला निष्पापमिर्मलि यरो॥ नपांपूजाद्ययरकयो॑तोना</Line>
        <Line>पष्येरसगामिनैरासर्व्वकामफलप्रदा मारकमनजाधिपद्य प्रदीपा त्रययस्सुखं। मह्यपदद्वजरु॥ नैवद्ययोकरद्यरस दीर्घापूर स्वाद्येरी</Line>
      </Paragraph>
    </Body>
  </Page>
</HistoricalDocument>

        <Line>کذر ایدر کن ناکهان بدونلی عربه جی حسین ایله پاپاس اوغلنه راست</Line>
        <Line>کلوب بونلر ایله بولوشوب مکر بونلر بر سفینه ایله یکرمی اوتوز قدر ار و</Line>
        <Line>عورت مسلمان اسیرلری دونمش و دونممش آلوب فوطوق قارشوسنده</Line>

        <Line>پاپاس اوغلی کتدی اما عربه جی حسینی صالیویرمدك اول کیجه قوناغمزده</Line>

<HistoricalDocument xmlns="http://example.com/historicaldocument">
  <Metadata>
    <Language>Turkish</Language>
    <WritingDirection>rtl</WritingDirection>
    <PhysicalDescription>Ink on paper.</PhysicalDescription>
    <Description>A page from the memoirs of Osman Agha of Timişoara, detailing experiences related to his captivity.</Description>
    <Script>Arabic</Script>
  </Metadata>
  <Page>
    <Body>
      <Paragraph>
        <Line>بونی كتور كوتور ديو ايش و غائله زیاده اولوب بعض دفعه بعضیلری</Line>
        <Line>سکا شو ایشی اصمار ليوب ديمشدم نيچون وجوده كتور مدك ديو</Line>
        <Line>شتم ايدوب ضرب ایلمکه بشلادیلر تموردن چیقوب خلاص اولدوغمه</Line>
        <Line>پشیمان اولدق لكن جنرالمزك بر حالی وار ایدی یاز ایاملرنده</Line>
        <Line>قلعه مزبورده اهل و اتباعیله کلوب اولوردی قیش وقتلرنده کنه ولایتی</Line>
        <Line>اولان اشتیر یا طرفلرینه غراج نام شهره و آندن کندو ملکلری اولان</Line>
        <Line>قافنبرغ قصبه سنه و قلعه سنه واروب مکث ایدرلردی چونکه قیش</Line>
        <Line>ایاملری دخول ایلدی جنرال ولایتنه كتمك اوزره تدارك اولندی بزم</Line>
        <Line>ایچون دخی کتخدامز تنبيه ايدوب ایوانیچ قلعه سندن واروژدینه وارنجه</Line>
        <Line>سن دخی عربه لر يا ننجه معاً كتمك لازم کلمشدر دیو امر ایدوب بز ایسه</Line>
        <Line>آندن ایچر و نمچه ولایتنه كتمكه غايت خوف ايدردك زيرا اكر ولايت</Line>
        <Line>مزبوره كتمك لازم كلورسه کیم بیلور بر دخی مسلمان ولایتنی قچن کورورز</Line>
        <Line>بزی آنده جبراً</Line>
      </Paragraph>
    </Body>
  </Page>
</HistoricalDocument>

      <Paragraph>

        <Line>رابع انکه شعور باحوال سلاطین و ذی الاحترام باعث ازدیاد عقل و وفور</Line>
        <Line>کیاست و صحت رای و اصابت تدبیر است از ابوز رچهر حکیم مروت</Line>
        <Line>که فرموده تاریخ سلاطین ممد رای صوابست چه علم باحوال سلف در</Line>
        <Line>صحت رای خلف دخیل عظیم دارد خامسا انکه سلاطین و پادشاهان را</Line>
        <Line>از دانستن احوال سلف اعتقاد بر قدرت قادر عظیم الشان</Line>

        <Line>را بقای نیست از تعاقب اقبال مغرور نگردند و از توالی ادبار محزون</Line>

        <Line>بود جمهر حکیم</Line>

        <Line>ایشان بر مکاره واقف کردد بلاشبه او را مرتبه صبر و رضا افزون</Line>
        <Line>شود این هر دو خصلت از اشرف خصایل حمیده است</Line>
